name: Intruder
summary: Intruder scans internet-facing and internal systems, cloud accounts and web apps, ranks findings with CVSS, CISA KEV and EPSS data, and pushes issues to Jira, GitHub, GitLab or ServiceNow. It has a free plan and a 14-day trial. Paid prices are not shown as numbers on the pricing page.

facts.text: Intruder says it finds new cloud services, subdomains and APIs and adds them to the platform automatically, and it can connect to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud accounts.
Findings are ranked using CVSS, CISA KEV and EPSS data.
Findings can be pushed to Jira, GitHub, GitLab or ServiceNow so a person can be assigned the fix, and Azure DevOps is listed in the FAQ.
The Free plan includes 5 infrastructure licenses and weekly external scans, but not web app or API scanning.
A license is used each time a target is scanned and stays used for 30 days. The 14-day trial includes Cloud features and 5 free licenses.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 5 infrastructure licenses, 3 users, weekly external scans

plans.name: Cloud
plans.notes: The pricing page shows no amount. The FAQ describes a base fee plus a small per-target fee

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Sales contact. The page shows no amount

hiddenCosts: Annual billing is shown as saving 20% against monthly billing, so the monthly rate costs more.
Prices exclude VAT. Invoice payment is offered only from 250 licenses.
AI pentests are a separate add-on starting from $3,500 per test.

contract.cancellation: Monthly contracts are rolling and can be cancelled at any time. Annual contracts carry an annual commitment.
